claim: `remove-page` can be refused by `folder-matches-a-shape` over the very folder its own answer empties, saying that folder holds no page of its own. The same act had landed six page removals of the same shape that day. `remove-property-value` on the parent's `parts` beside a bare `remove-folder` landed what `remove-page` would not, so the work is reachable by another route and the refusal is in the reading of the folder rather than in the edits.

evidence:
Over `change/mechanical/file-content/remove/remove-page-property`, a change page with a code file and a test file beside it. I ran `akasha change draft remove-page` with `at:` that page and then `akasha change apply`, at `4271bfe547a`. The draft answered four lines: it changed the parent domain `change-mechanical-file-content-remove.domain.ts`, and took the page, its code and its test away. The apply refused:

`change/mechanical/file-content/remove/remove-page-property — this folder matches no folder shape — as a-claimed-folder, no page above it claims this folder; as a-domain-with-its-parts, it holds no page of its own; as a-page-type-with-its-parts, it holds no page of its own; as a-page-with-its-parts, it holds no page of its own; …`

The answer removed every file the path index lists under that folder. `.index/path/changes/mechanical/file-content/remove/remove-page-property/` held exactly three rows, one for each of the three files the answer removed, so nothing the index knows was left. I ran the same apply three times and it refused identically each time. Adding an `akasha change draft remove-folder` edit for the folder alongside the page removal did not settle it either: the fourth apply refused with the same line for the same folder.

That same hour the same act landed six removals of folders of the same shape, each a change page with code and test beside it: `948d0444fc5`, `ee89bff5844`, `1fe8de28f29`, `1068196c0ca`, `9951ff6fed9`, `246a482d624`. The one thing that differed at `remove-page-property` is that its git-ignored `…entries.uncommitted.jsonl` had already been taken off the disk by an earlier apply rather than in the same answer, so the answer carried three removes where the six that worked carried four.

What landed instead, as `ec245ca8893`: `akasha change draft remove-property-value` with `at:` the parent domain, `key: parts`, `value: change-mechanical-file-content/remove-page-property`, then `akasha change draft remove-folder` with `at:` the folder, then one apply. Those two drafts answer the same edits `remove-page` answers, and the apply was not refused.

What this means is for whoever picks it up. It could be that the check reads the folder from the tree rather than from the answer and `remove-folder` is what sweeps the directory; it could be that an answer removing every file of a folder without also removing an untracked file the folder held leaves the folder there in the reading. I did not mend the act.
